memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: You shall not covet your neighbor's wife. You shall not set your desire on your neighbor's house or land, his male or female servant, his ox or donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor. - Deut 5:21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The final commandment is unique among the ten because it deals entirely with the heart. The others can be seen — stealing, lying, murder. But coveting hides inside us, unseen by anyone but God. To covet is to burn with desire for what belongs to someone else: their spouse, their home, their possessions, their life. It is the restless craving that whispers, "If only I had what they have, then I would be satisfied."

This command exposes something profound: sin is not only about our actions but about the desires of our hearts. That is why the tenth commandment quietly convicts every one of us. Who has never looked at another's life with a pang of envy? Coveting reveals that our real battle is a discontented heart that refuses to trust God's good provision.

The answer to coveting is not gritting our teeth but a transformed heart — one that finds its treasure in Christ. Paul learned "to be content whatever the circumstances" because his sufficiency was in Jesus, not in his possessions (Phil 4:11-13). When Christ becomes our greatest treasure, the endless craving loosens its grip, because we already possess the One who satisfies. True contentment is not having everything; it is having Him. Ask God to make your heart restful and grateful today, satisfied in His love above all else.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What do I find myself coveting — and what does that reveal about my heart?
- Do I believe that Christ is a greater treasure than anything I lack?
- How can I cultivate genuine contentment and gratitude this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You see the desires hidden in my heart. Free me from restless coveting, and teach me the deep contentment that comes from treasuring Jesus above every earthly thing. Let Him be enough for me. Amen.
